title: Put a silicone swimming cap onto a headform
instruction: Stretch the swimming cap over the headform. Cover the crown, leave the face clear, and release it without tearing the cap.
setup: An upright adult headform, 190 x 160 x 240 mm, fixed to the table. A separate silicone cap has a 168 x 160 mm opening, 90 mm dome, 0.8 mm sheet and 3 mm rolled rim. It starts dome-up on a fixed wooden rest 20 cm in front of the head: a 100 mm diameter, 110 mm high cylinder on a 140 x 140 x 15 mm base. The loose rim is accessible from both sides. Both grippers have 40 x 12 x 3 mm finger extensions. Restore the photographed layout.
scoring: 1.0 if the intact cap covers the crown, its rim surrounds the head below the crown and above the eyes, and it stays fitted for three seconds after release. The crown gap must be at most 2 cm; the rim must stay within the 5.5 cm below to 7.5 cm above head-centre band, with the front edge at least 3 cm above head centre. 0.5 for the surrounding rim and clear face without the crown/release condition; 0.25 for the crown within 2.5 cm and face clear. Otherwise 0. A torn cap scores 0. Use the video and a ruler.
fidelity: The cap is an elastic shell with self-contact and a rolled rim. A pinch uses a native constraint only when the rim is between closing finger faces; it releases on opening and breaks at 18 N or 0.08 Nm. Material response is approximate and the head is rigid. The robot must stretch, place and release the cap; no fitted shape is prescribed. Grip reaction loads on the robot are omitted.
scores: Development diagnostics only; no validated full-score demonstration or Dream baseline yet.
context: Fitting a swimming cap requires stretching a thin elastic object around a curved surface while keeping the face clear.
